# Bibliography

<!-- AUTO-GENERATED by docs/fetch_papers.py. Edit the list in that file, not here. -->

Every entry below is downloadable with `python docs/fetch_papers.py`.
PDFs land in `docs/pdf/` and are gitignored, so the repository stays small.

Each `Why` line states what decision in `backend/` the paper supports.
That is the only reason a paper is in this list.

## Leakage

Evaluation honesty: signer independence, splits, and shortcut learning.
These are the papers that justify why this project refuses a random split.

### American Sign Language fingerspelling recognition from video: Methods for unrestricted recognition and signer-independence

Taehwan Kim (2016-08-30). [arXiv:1608.08339](https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.08339).

**Why:** The reference statement of the signer-independence problem. Reports letter error rates near 60% once the test signer is unseen, against near-perfect numbers when they are not. The gap this project measures.

### Signer-independent Fingerspelling Recognition with Deep Neural Network Adaptation

Taehwan Kim, Weiran Wang, Hao Tang et al. (2016-02-13). [arXiv:1602.04278](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.04278).

**Why:** Signer adaptation as an explicit step, which only makes sense once you accept that signer identity is a confound rather than noise.

### Shortcut Learning in Deep Neural Networks

Robert Geirhos, Jörn-Henrik Jacobsen, Claudio Michaelis et al. (2020-04-16). [arXiv:2004.07780](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.07780).

**Why:** Geirhos et al. The general theory of why a model scores 99.9% on a benchmark and fails on a phone photo: it solved an easier problem that the benchmark accidentally rewarded.

### ImageNet-trained CNNs are biased towards texture; increasing shape bias improves accuracy and robustness

Robert Geirhos, Patricia Rubisch, Claudio Michaelis et al. (2018-11-29). [arXiv:1811.12231](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.12231).

**Why:** Concrete evidence that vision models latch onto texture and background statistics. Motivates the aggressive colour/grayscale augmentation in `data.build_transforms` and the planned hand-crop step.

### Toward American Sign Language Processing in the Real World: Data, Tasks, and Methods

Bowen Shi (2023-08-23). [arXiv:2308.12419](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.12419).

**Why:** Shi et al. on the gap between curated ASL corpora and deployment, and the data/task design needed to close it.

## Datasets

The corpora themselves: what exists, how it was collected, and who signed it.

### A New 27 Class Sign Language Dataset Collected from 173 Individuals

Arda Mavi, Zeynep Dikle (2022-03-08). [arXiv:2203.03859](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.03859).

**Why:** Mavi & Dikle. The static ASL corpus with genuine signer diversity (173 volunteers), and the reason `asl_27class` is in the registry.

### FSboard: Over 3 million characters of ASL fingerspelling collected via smartphones

Manfred Georg, Garrett Tanzer, Saad Hassan et al. (2024-07-22). [arXiv:2407.15806](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.15806).

**Why:** 3M+ characters of ASL fingerspelling captured on smartphones by 147 signers. The closest public data to this project's actual deployment condition: a phone camera held by the signer.

### Sign-Language Datasets at Scale: A Comprehensive Survey on Resources, Benchmarks, and Annotation Standards

Yiming Ni, Zhi-Qi Cheng, Jiayu Li et al. (2026-04-28). [arXiv:2606.19352](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19352).

**Why:** Survey of sign-language resources, benchmarks, and annotation standards. Use it to check a corpus before adding it to the registry.

### Isharah: A Large-Scale Multi-Scene Dataset for Continuous Sign Language Recognition

Sarah Alyami, Hamzah Luqman, Sadam Al-Azani et al. (2025-06-04). [arXiv:2506.03615](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.03615).

**Why:** Large multi-scene continuous corpus. Multi-scene is the property that makes cross-condition evaluation possible at all.

### AUTSL: A Large Scale Multi-modal Turkish Sign Language Dataset and Baseline Methods

Ozge Mercanoglu Sincan, Hacer Yalim Keles (2020-08-03). [arXiv:2008.00932](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.00932).

**Why:** AUTSL, with an explicit signer-independent benchmark protocol worth copying.

### BSL-1K: Scaling up co-articulated sign language recognition using mouthing cues

Samuel Albanie, Gül Varol, Liliane Momeni et al. (2020-07-23). [arXiv:2007.12131](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.12131).

**Why:** Scaling isolated sign recognition via mouthing cues, and a careful discussion of how episode-level splits avoid leakage.

### A HamNoSys-Guided Dataset and Baselines for Fine-Grained Isolated Handshape Recognition in Sign Language

Ushnish Sarkar, Suvajit Patra, Bhaswar Chattopadhyay et al. (2026-08-11). [arXiv:2608.10588](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10588).

**Why:** Fine-grained isolated handshape recognition. Handshape is exactly what a still photo can carry, so this is the closest task to ours.

## Transformers

Vision transformers: the backbone, how to fine-tune it, and how to read it.

### An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale

Alexey Dosovitskiy, Lucas Beyer, Alexander Kolesnikov et al. (2020-10-22). [arXiv:2010.11929](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.11929).

**Why:** Dosovitskiy et al. The architecture. Note the data-hunger finding, which is why every preset here starts from ImageNet-21k weights.

### How to train your ViT? Data, Augmentation, and Regularization in Vision Transformers

Andreas Steiner, Alexander Kolesnikov, Xiaohua Zhai et al. (2021-06-18). [arXiv:2106.10270](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.10270).

**Why:** Steiner et al. The augreg study behind the exact checkpoints in `model.PRESETS`, and the source of the augmentation-vs-data tradeoffs that matter on corpora this small.

### Training data-efficient image transformers & distillation through attention

Hugo Touvron, Matthieu Cord, Matthijs Douze et al. (2020-12-23). [arXiv:2012.12877](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.12877).

**Why:** Training ViTs without hundreds of millions of images. The recipe this project's training loop is a stripped-down version of.

### DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision

Maxime Oquab, Timothée Darcet, Théo Moutakanni et al. (2023-04-14). [arXiv:2304.07193](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07193).

**Why:** Self-supervised features that transfer without task-specific fine-tuning. The `dinov2_small` preset exists to test whether self-supervised pretraining survives the cross-corpus jump better.

### Quantifying Attention Flow in Transformers

Samira Abnar, Willem Zuidema (2020-05-02). [arXiv:2005.00928](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.00928).

**Why:** Abnar & Zuidema. Attention rollout, implemented in `model.attention_rollout`. Raw per-layer attention is misleading because of the residual stream; rollout corrects for it.

## Slr Methods

Applied sign-language recognition with attention architectures. The direct
comparison points, several of which report the inflated numbers this project
is designed to contextualise.

### Continuous Saudi Sign Language Recognition: A Vision Transformer Approach

Soukeina Elhassen, Lama Al Khuzayem, Areej Alhothali et al. (2025-09-03). [arXiv:2509.03467](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.03467).

**Why:** Continuous Saudi sign language with a ViT. Recent, and a useful check on how the field currently reports splits.

### Breaking the Barriers: Video Vision Transformers for Word-Level Sign Language Recognition

Alexander Brettmann, Jakob Grävinghoff, Marlene Rüschoff et al. (2025-04-10). [arXiv:2504.07792](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07792).

**Why:** Video ViTs for word-level recognition; the temporal counterpart to what we do on stills.

### Stack Transformer Based Spatial-Temporal Attention Model for Dynamic Sign Language and Fingerspelling Recognition

Koki Hirooka, Abu Saleh Musa Miah, Tatsuya Murakami et al. (2025-03-21). [arXiv:2503.16855](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.16855).

**Why:** Stacked spatial-temporal attention for dynamic signs and fingerspelling.

### HandReader: Advanced Techniques for Efficient Fingerspelling Recognition

Pavel Korotaev, Petr Surovtsev, Alexander Kapitanov et al. (2025-05-15). [arXiv:2505.10267](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10267).

**Why:** Efficient fingerspelling recognition; relevant to the on-device latency budget.

### Fingerspelling PoseNet: Enhancing Fingerspelling Translation with Pose-Based Transformer Models

Pooya Fayyazsanavi, Negar Nejatishahidin, Jana Kosecka (2023-11-20). [arXiv:2311.12128](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12128).

**Why:** Pose-based transformer. The main architectural alternative to raw pixels, and the reason hand cropping is the planned next step.

### A Fine-Grained Visual Attention Approach for Fingerspelling Recognition in the Wild

Kamala Gajurel, Cuncong Zhong, Guanghui Wang (2021-05-17). [arXiv:2105.07625](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.07625).

**Why:** Attention over the hand region in the wild - the published version of the crop-the-hand idea marked as future work in `data.py`.

### A Comparative Analysis of Recurrent and Attention Architectures for Isolated Sign Language Recognition

Nigar Alishzade, Gulchin Abdullayeva (2025-11-17). [arXiv:2511.13126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.13126).

**Why:** Direct architectural comparison on isolated SLR; a sanity check on whether attention is worth its cost here.

## Deployment

Calibration and abstention: turning a classifier into something an app can
responsibly show a user.

### On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks

Chuan Guo, Geoff Pleiss, Yu Sun et al. (2017-06-14). [arXiv:1706.04599](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.04599).

**Why:** Guo et al. Modern networks are overconfident; temperature scaling fixes it with one parameter. Implemented in `evaluate.fit_temperature`.

### Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks

Yonatan Geifman, Ran El-Yaniv (2017-05-23). [arXiv:1705.08500](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.08500).

**Why:** Geifman & El-Yaniv. The risk-coverage framing behind the abstention threshold the API serves.

## Not on arXiv

These are worth reading but are behind publisher paywalls, so only the link is recorded.

- [HGR-ViT: Hand Gesture Recognition with Vision Transformer](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10303839/) (Sensors, 2023).
  Reports 99.98% on the ASL alphabet. Read it as the clearest example of what a
  random split buys you, and compare against the cross-corpus numbers this
  project produces on the same data.
- [FluentSigners-50: A signer independent benchmark dataset](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0273649) (PLOS ONE, 2022).
  A benchmark built signer-independent from the start; the protocol worth imitating.
- [SignViT: an enhanced vision transformer framework](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1746809425011139)
  (Biomedical Signal Processing and Control, 2025).
- [Investigating Signer-Independent Sign Language Recognition on LSA64](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/363174384) (2022).
